title: Eight MGNREGA Workers Killed as Speeding Car Rams Roadside Crew in Sangrur
excerpt: The labourers were on a water break beside the Lehragaga-Jakhal road in Punjab when the car struck a motorcyclist and ploughed into the group; witnesses say ambulances took nearly an hour to arrive.
body:
• Eight MGNREGA labourers were killed and 12 injured on Sunday when a speeding car ploughed into a crew resting beside the Lehragaga-Jakhal road near Alisher village in Punjab's Sangrur district, police and district officials said.
  • Witnesses said ambulances took nearly an hour to reach the scene; residents blocked the road in protest, and officials have not confirmed the delay.
  • Police identified the driver as Pargat Singh Kala, who fled after the crash; a case has been registered and raids are under way to arrest him.
  • Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann announced compensation of ₹2 lakh for each victim's family and said the government will cover the injured workers' medical expenses.

Eight labourers working under India's rural employment guarantee scheme were killed and 12 others injured on Sunday afternoon after a speeding car rammed into the group as they took a water break beside a road in Punjab's Sangrur district, police said. Five workers died at the scene and three succumbed to their injuries in hospital, according to The Times of India, which named all eight victims — every one of them a resident of Alisher village, near where the crash occurred.

What Happened

The crash occurred at around 3:30 p.m. on the Lehragaga-Jakhal road near Alisher village, about 50 km from Sangrur town, Senior Medical Officer Dr Vinod Kumar said. A crew of 23 labourers employed under the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) was working on a road project and had paused by the roadside to drink water.

https://x.com/DDNewslive/status/2111836568688435210

Witnesses told The Times of India that a sedan travelling from Jakhal first struck a motorcyclist parked along the road and then ploughed into the workers. India Today identified the vehicle as a Chevrolet Magnum with a Patiala registration and named the driver as Pargat Singh Kala, a resident of Raidhrana. The driver fled the scene; other occupants of the car were apprehended at the spot, police said.

The dead were identified as Karamjit Kaur, Jeevan Singh, Nikki, Sarabjit Kaur, Ranjit Begum, Karamjit, Rani Kaur and Desraj — all residents of Alisher village. The injured were taken to Rajindra Hospital in Patiala, with the seriously hurt referred to Sangrur Civil Hospital.

There was one conflicting official count late on Sunday. Inspector Jaskaran Singh, the Lehragaga station house officer, told news agency ANI that nine people had lost their lives. The district administration put the toll at eight dead and 12 injured, the figure also reported by Livemint.

Witnesses Say the Ambulance Came Too Late

Eyewitnesses and survivors said the wait for ambulances stretched to nearly an hour, and NDTV reported that some of the injured died before help arrived. Officials have not confirmed the alleged delay.

"We were sitting on the road and drinking water... A car rammed into us... Some people died in the accident."

— Injured worker, speaking to ANI

Anger over the response spilled onto the road. Local residents blocked the Lehragaga-Jakhal road in protest, alleging that ambulances arrived late; as Dainik Jagran reported, residents also questioned delays in police assistance. The blockade was lifted after senior police officers assured protesters of strict action.

Driver on the Run; Government Announces Compensation

Superintendent of Police Palwinder Singh Cheema said an investigation is under way and a first information report is being registered, and he assured protesters of strict legal action against the accused for rash and negligent driving. Police said raids were being conducted to arrest Kala.

Deputy Commissioner Poonamdeep Kaur said the district administration would provide medical aid and all possible assistance to the victims and their families. Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann, in a post on X, said the families of the deceased will receive compensation of ₹2 lakh each and that the state will bear the cost of treatment for the injured. Cabinet Minister Barinder Kumar Goyal also offered condolences. Congress leader Amarinder Singh Raja Warring described the victims as "the lowest paid workers who work hard for their livelihood" and pressed for medical assistance, strict punishment and proper compensation.

Roadside Crews With Little Protection

MGNREGA guarantees rural households up to 100 days of wage employment a year and is among India's lowest-paid forms of public work; its crews routinely labour on or beside live carriageways. Survivors of Sunday's crash told reporters there were no warning signs, reflectors or barricades at the work site and that the crew had not been given safety jackets — an account officials have not yet addressed publicly.

Two questions now sit with the district administration: how the police investigation assigns responsibility for the crash, and whether the deaths prompt a review of work-zone safety for road crews and of ambulance response times on rural routes. The condition of the 12 injured workers, several of them seriously hurt, will be the next update.
